full_judgment: 8. In this matter Mr. Younus Halder already argued the case on behalf of the petitioner. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel, appears today and submits that this is not the proper stage of the proceeding to implead the opposite patty No. 2 as plaintiff. He has argued that a letter of request was issued by the learned Court by order dated 8-11-79 for examining the said Pran Ballav and by that it will be ascertained whether the original plaintiff Pran Ballav is alive or dead and that order on challenge by Malati Sarker was upheld upto the High Court Division. But no report against letter of request has yet been sent to the trial Court, and in view of that unless that portion of the proceeding is exhausted the opposite party No. 2 has no legal footing to be impleaded as plaintiff in the suit. His further contention is that if any report is sent against that letter of request by the District Judge, 24 Parganas showing that Pran Ballav is dead, in that case Malati Sarker, the daughter of the original plaintiff will again be substituted and brought on record as plaintiff in due course to proceed with the suit. Mr. Fazlul Karim submits that there is still possibility of Malati Sarker being substituted in the suit, and as such, without exhausting rule 3 of Order 22 of the Code the court should not have resorted to apply Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in making the opposite party No. 2 as plaintiff in the suit. In support of this contention the learned Counsel has made reliance on the decisions in the case of Kedarnath Kanoria and ors vs. Khatian Sons & Co. reported in AIR 1959 (Cal) 368 and Gautarn De Sitamany vs. Madhavan Sivarajan, reported in AIR 1977 Kerala 83.
